diagnosis: I calibrated HBV on daily flow from 1971-10 to 1997-12, maximising NSE, after treating the first water year as warm-up. The search method was DDS (5,500 runs in two stages), and I set the starting store levels to their typical long-run values. Fit: NSE 0.797, KGE 0.82, PBIAS +3.9%, r 0.89. Main parameters: FC about 373 mm, LP 0.97, BETA 4.2, quick fast-flow response (K0 0.92, K1 0.50, UZL 25 mm), PERC 4 mm/day, K2 0.12, MAXBAS 2.5 days. Snow matters little (about 5% of precipitation falls as snow); SFCF is about 0.9 and two snow parameters, CFR and CWH, sit at their lower bound of 0, which is physically reasonable. A second DDS search from a different start and seed reached a clearly different optimum (FC 181 mm, LP 0.44, BETA 1.3) with a lower NSE of 0.784. So the soil parameters are equifinal and only weakly identified, while flow-routing timing is more consistent. Likely weak points: the largest flood peaks (simulated maximum 26.5 vs observed 29.7 mm/day), timing errors in convective summer storms, and low flows. Two small reservoirs in the catchment and some groundwater in the aquifers may also cause errors the model does not capture. I did not run a split-sample validation, so I have no independent test. I am moderately confident; I'd expect NSE of about 0.72–0.80 in 1998–2008 if the climate stays similar.
